_README: Classified divergences for the AU/AMT arm of the A/B, keyed by assertion
UUID. Same contract as ci/known-engine-divergences.json: an unlisted
divergence fails the gate, and a listed one that stops diverging also fails,
because a baseline nobody prunes stops describing anything.
This file exists separately because the AU arm runs a different corpus (the
360 international assertions plus the 200 AMT ones) against a different
release, so a cause proven here does not transfer to the international
nightly and must not be smuggled into its baseline.
WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, 2026-09-10. Three assertions diverged on the 894MB
AU release (amtv4-15912.zip). Only ONE of them belongs in a baseline; the
other two were artefacts of HOW the run was submitted, and are recorded here
as directions rather than allowances so that re-appearing after the
configuration is fixed is a failure and not a shrug.
1. 17b6c41e - MySQL 1,405,850 findings, DuckDB not-run.
2. fc0f240c - MySQL 8 findings, DuckDB not-run.
Both are the SAME cause: an AU extension is a dependent release, and this run
supplied no dependency. MySQL substitutes an absent schema and compares
against nothing, which is how one assertion produced 1.4M rows - a finding
per language refset member in the edition. DuckDB skips statements naming
<DEPENDENCY> and says so. Supplying --dependency-release removes both, and
until the AU arm does, its numbers are not a parity measurement. Neither is
listed as an allowance: fix the submission, do not baseline it.
fc0f240c is also the reason this file exists at all. MySQL's 8 findings are
REAL - verified by hand against the isa closure, attributetype
900000000000469006 has 7 ancestors and 707000009 is not among them - and
DuckDB reported 0 and PASSED. Of that assertion's 12 statements exactly one
writes to qa_result and exactly that one needs the dependency, so 11
statements ran, none could report, and the run looked clean. The engine now
reports not-run when every qa_result writer was skipped, which is what turns
this from a silent false negative into divergence 2 above. See
DuckDbAssertionExecutionServiceTest#anAssertionWhoseOnlyFindingWriterIsSkippedIsNotRunRatherThanPassed.

directions.candidate-higher: DuckDB reports more failures than MySQL for an assertion
directions.incumbent-higher: MySQL reports more failures than DuckDB for an assertion

5451f5c6-13c2-76a5-3590-fb889ae6a29f.directionNote: MySQL -1 against DuckDB 0, so the arithmetic reads as candidate-higher. The sentinel is the whole difference: MySQL abandoned the assertion on a missing table and DuckDB ran it against the empty one the store declares.
5451f5c6-13c2-76a5-3590-fb889ae6a29f.appliesTo: Full ccsRefset validation - 01, on any release that does not ship a ccsRefset file
5451f5c6-13c2-76a5-3590-fb889ae6a29f.observed: MySQL failureCount -1 in assertionsFailed with 'Table rvf_au_20260831_<runid>.ccsRefset_f doesn't exist'; DuckDB 0 in assertionsPassed
cause: CORRECTED 2026-09-11. The cause recorded here was wrong, and the wrong
cause pointed at the release instead of at one word of SQL.
It said the AU release ships no ccsRefset file, so MySQL never creates the
table. MySQL creates every table in create-tables-mysql.sql when it builds
the schema, whatever the release contains, and that DDL declares
ccsrefset_f. The table is there.
What is not there is `ccsRefset_f`. The assertion asks for
`<PROSPECTIVE>.ccsRefset_<FULL>` in camel case, the schema declares
`ccsrefset_f` in lower case, and MySQL compares table names
case-sensitively wherever lower_case_table_names = 0 - the default on
Linux. So the statement dies on a table that does not exist, reports
failureCount -1, and reads as a release that failed to ship a file.
DuckDB resolves identifiers case-insensitively and finds the table, which
is the entire divergence.
Why it survived: MySQL on macOS and Windows lower-cases table names by
default, so only a Linux MySQL sees it, and only for the one name in 1,107
assertion files that is spelled differently. ci/assertion_lint.py --ddl now
finds it, and ci/pr/amt/ carries the one-word fix.
PROVEN: with `ccsRefset_<FULL>` changed to `ccsrefset_<FULL>` and the pack
republished, the AMT fixture arm reports 267 of 267 identical, 0 divergent,
and MySQL's incomplete count goes from 1 to 0. This entry retires when that
fix lands upstream.
5451f5c6-13c2-76a5-3590-fb889ae6a29f.evidence: Verified 2026-09-10 against amtv4-15912.zip: 0 zip entries matching ccsRefset, store.json tableColumns declares ccsrefset_f/_s/_d
5451f5c6-13c2-76a5-3590-fb889ae6a29f.moveWhen: The AU release starts shipping a ccsRefset file, at which point both engines read the same rows and this entry must be removed

_README: Assertions one engine reports that do not join to the other by
assertionUuid. Zero is the target on the international arm; the AU arm
cannot reach zero until the dependency release is supplied, because a
not-run item and an incomplete are both reported but neither carries a
comparable count.
